studies.officialTitle: A Phase 1, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single and Multiple Ascending Dose Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of VK2735, a Dual Glucagon-like Peptide-1 and Gastric Inhibitory Polypeptide Receptor Agonist, in Healthy Adults and Otherwise Healthy Adults Who Have an Increased Body Mass Index

design.description: Three-part single and multiple ascending dose study: Part A (single subcutaneous dose, healthy participants), Part B (subcutaneous doses once weekly for 4 weeks, healthy or increased-BMI participants), and Part C (oral doses once daily for 28 days, participants with obesity, BMI >=30 kg/m^2). Only Parts B and C had disclosed arm-level weight or safety results; Part A produced no disclosed arm-level weight or safety breakdown and is not separately modeled here. Schema limitation: this single registry identifier and Study record spans both the subcutaneous (Part B) and oral (Part C) routes of the same asset, but the contract permits only one programId per Study. This Study is anchored to the oral-tablet program (viking-therapeutics-vk2735-oral-tablet) because Part C is the part whose enrolled population most clearly satisfies the Evidence Scope obesity criterion; its Part B (subcutaneous) results are consequently not reciprocally discoverable from the subcutaneous-injection program's own page. This is not modeled by creating a duplicate Study or a surrogate registry id; it is reported here as a REVIEW_REQUIRED schema-boundary case per the workflow's case-scoped fallback.

studies.population: Healthy adults, and otherwise healthy adults with an increased body mass index, receiving single or multiple ascending subcutaneous doses (Parts A and B); adults with obesity (BMI >=30 kg/m^2) receiving multiple ascending oral doses (Part C).
studies.safetySummary: Across the subcutaneous multiple-ascending-dose cohorts (Part B), nausea (33-83% of VK2735 cohorts vs. 50% placebo) and vomiting (0-33% vs. 10% placebo) were the most common adverse events, without a clear dose-response pattern disclosed at the individual-cohort level; one serious adverse event (acute choledocholithiasis in a participant with a prior gallstone history) occurred, and no discontinuations due to gastrointestinal adverse events were reported. In the oral multiple-dose cohorts (Part C), nausea occurred in 14% of VK2735-treated participants (pooled across active doses) versus 0% with placebo, and vomiting occurred in 0% of both groups; no serious adverse events were reported.

studies.officialTitle: A Phase 2 Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, 13-week Study of VK2735 for Weight Management in Subjects Who Are Obese, or Overweight With at Least One Weight-related Comorbid Condition

design.description: Parallel-group, dose-ranging trial of once-weekly subcutaneous VK2735 versus placebo over 13 weeks, with dose titration for the 5 mg, 10 mg, and 15 mg arms.

studies.population: Adults who are obese (BMI >=30 kg/m^2) or overweight (BMI >=27 kg/m^2, <50 kg/m^2) with at least one weight-related comorbid condition, without diabetes mellitus.
studies.safetySummary: Gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation) were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events and generally increased with dose. Twelve treatment-emergent serious adverse events occurred in eight participants overall; ten were assessed as unrelated to study drug and two (atrial fibrillation and dehydration, both in one 5 mg participant) as possibly or probably related. One death occurred in the 15 mg arm (head trauma from a fall, assessed as unrelated to study drug); no Grade 4/5 treatment-related adverse events occurred. Discontinuation due to adverse events, chiefly nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and headache, ranged from 0% (placebo) to 20% (15 mg).

studies.officialTitle: A Phase 2 Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, 13-week Dose Finding Study of VK2735 Oral Formulation for Weight Management in Subjects Who Are Obese, or Overweight With at Least One Weight-related Comorbid Condition

design.description: Parallel-group, dose-ranging trial of once-daily oral VK2735 tablet versus placebo over 13 weeks, with dose titration for the 60 mg, 90 mg, and 120 mg arms and a maintenance/de-escalation cohort titrated up to 90 mg before stepping down to a 30 mg maintenance dose.

studies.population: Adults (>=18 years) who are obese (BMI >=30 kg/m^2) or overweight (BMI >=27 kg/m^2, <50 kg/m^2) with at least one weight-related comorbid condition (hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, or cardiovascular disease); no current or past type 2 diabetes diagnosis.
studies.safetySummary: Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events, with 98% of drug-related and 99% of GI-specific adverse events assessed as mild or moderate. Discontinuation due to adverse events occurred in 13% of placebo participants versus a pooled 20% (range approximately 8-20% across active dose arms) of VK2735 participants; overall discontinuation was 18% (placebo) versus a pooled 28% (range approximately 20-38%) for VK2735. Diarrhea (up to 25%) and constipation (up to 43%) were also reported across active doses, not itemized per arm. Serious adverse events and anti-drug antibody incidence were not reported in the available sources.
